question: A cheetah is ______ than a lion. 🐆
explanation: Great job! When comparing two animals, we add '-er' to the word. So, fast becomes faster! ⚡
hint: Look for the word ending in '-er'.

question: A snail is ______ than a turtle. 🐌
explanation: Super! We use '-er' to compare two things. Slow changes to slower. 🐌

question: The giraffe is the ______ animal in the zoo. 🦒
explanation: Awesome! When comparing three or more things, we use '-est'. The giraffe is the tallest! 🦒
hint: Look for the word ending in '-est'.

question: My pencil is ______ than yours. ✏️
explanation: Fantastic! We are comparing two pencils, so we add '-er' to make it shorter. ✏️

question: An elephant is ______ than a dog. 🐘
explanation: Brilliant! To compare two animals, big becomes bigger. We double the 'g' here! 🐘
hint: Look for the word with double 'g' and '-er'.

question: An ant is ______ than a bee. 🐜
explanation: Wonderful! We add '-er' when comparing the size of two bugs. 🐜

question: Ice cream is ______ than hot chocolate. 🍦
explanation: Yummy! You got it! Comparing two treats means we use colder. 🍦

question: The sun is ______ than a campfire. ☀️
explanation: Spot on! We double the 't' and add '-er' to compare two hot things. ☀️
hint: Look for the word with double 't' and '-er'.

question: She is ______ today than she was yesterday. 😊
explanation: Super! When a word ends in 'y', we change the 'y' to 'i' and add '-er'. 😊

question: This lightbulb is ______ than the old one. 💡
explanation: Great job! Comparing two lights means we add '-er' to bright. 💡

question: Mount Everest is the ______ mountain in the world. ⛰️
explanation: Awesome! Comparing all mountains means we use the '-est' form. ⛰️
hint: Look for the word ending in '-est'.

question: The baby is the ______ person in our family. 👶
explanation: Fantastic! We use youngest when comparing all family members. 👶

question: The blue whale is the ______ animal on Earth. 🐋
explanation: Super! When it is the top one of all, we use the '-est' word. Biggest is right! 🐋

question: A mouse is the ______ animal in the room. 🐁
explanation: Brilliant! We add '-est' to small to show it is the tiny one of the whole group. 🐁

question: This is the ______ kite in the sky! 🪁
explanation: Awesome! To show it's at the very top of all kites, we use highest. 🪁

question: That was the ______ sound I ever heard! 📢
explanation: Great job! Out of all sounds, the top one gets an '-est' at the end. 📢

question: The library is the ______ place in the school. 📚
explanation: Wonderful! We add '-est' to quiet because we are comparing all places in the school. 📚

question: My sister is the ______ girl in her class. 🧠
explanation: Spot on! Comparing her to the whole class means we use smartest! 🎓

question: This is the ______ car in the race! 🏎️
explanation: Super! Out of all the cars, this one wins with '-est'. Quickest! 🏎️

question: Grandpa is the ______ person I know. 👴
explanation: Fantastic! When comparing everyone you know, use oldest. 👴

question: My bag is ______ than yours. 🎒
explanation: Awesome! We change 'y' to 'i' and add '-er' to compare two heavy bags. 🎒

question: A feather is ______ than a coin. 🪶
explanation: Great job! Comparing two things means we use lighter. 🪶

question: That joke was ______ than the first one. 😂
explanation: Brilliant! We change 'y' to 'i' and add '-er' to compare two jokes. 🤣

question: Today is a ______ day than yesterday. 🍀
explanation: Super! When a word ends in 'y', change it to 'i' and add '-er'. 🍀

question: This math puzzle is ______ than the reading puzzle. 🧩
explanation: Awesome! Comparing two puzzles means we use easier (change y to i + er). ✅

question: A rock is ______ than a pillow. 🪨
explanation: Fantastic! We add '-er' to compare two items. Harder is correct! 🪨

question: A bunny is ______ than a lizard. 🐰
explanation: Wonderful! We add '-er' to soft to compare the two animals. 🐰

question: Honey is ______ than bread. 🍯
explanation: Spot on! Comparing two foods means we use sweeter. 🍯

question: This apple is ______ than that apple. 🍎
explanation: Great job! To compare two apples, we add '-er' to make fresher. 🍎

question: Your room is ______ than my room! 🛏️
explanation: Awesome! Comparing two rooms means we use neater. ✨

question: Eating fruit is ______ than eating candy. 🍎
explanation: Super! 'Good' is a special word. When we compare two things, it changes completely to 'better'. 🌟
hint: Good changes to a completely new word when comparing two things.

question: She is the ______ singer in the school choir. 🎤
explanation: Brilliant! 'Good' changes to 'best' when we compare more than two people. 🏆

question: Getting a cold is ______ than getting a small scratch. 🤧
explanation: Fantastic! 'Bad' is a special word. It changes to 'worse' when comparing two things. 🤒
hint: 'Bad' changes to a special word starting with 'W' to compare two things.

question: That was the ______ storm of the year! ⛈️
explanation: Awesome! When 'bad' describes the top level out of all, it changes to 'worst'. 🌪️

question: The park is ______ from here than the store. 🏞️
explanation: Great job! 'Far' is a special word. It changes to 'farther' when comparing two distances. 🚴

question: Pluto is the ______ planet from the sun. 🪐
explanation: Super! When comparing all distances, 'far' changes to 'farthest'. 🌌
hint: Look for the special word ending in '-est'.

question: The ocean is ______ than the lake. 🌊
explanation: Wonderful! We add '-er' to deep to compare two bodies of water. 🤿

question: This is the ______ part of the swimming pool. 🏊‍♂️
explanation: Spot on! We add '-est' to show it's the very bottom of the whole pool. ⚓

question: My hands are ______ than yours after washing them. 🧼
explanation: Brilliant! We add '-er' to compare two clean things. 🧴

question: This is the ______ shirt in the closet. 👕
explanation: Awesome! Out of all the shirts, this one gets the '-est' ending. ✨

question: A butterfly is ______ than a moth. 🦋
explanation: Fantastic! For long words like colorful, we use 'more' to compare two things. 🦋
hint: Use 'more' in front of the long word.

question: The rainbow is the ______ thing in the sky. 🌈
explanation: Great job! For long words compared in a whole group, we use 'most'. 🌈
hint: Use 'most' in front of the long word.

question: A peacock is ______ than a pigeon. 🦚
explanation: Super! Beautiful is a long word, so we put 'more' in front to compare two birds. ✨
hint: Use 'more' for comparing two things with a long word.

question: She wore the ______ dress at the party! 👗
explanation: Awesome! When picking the top one out of all, we use 'most' with long words. 👑
hint: Use 'most' for the top level with long words.

question: My teacher is ______ than a dictionary! 👩‍🏫
explanation: Wonderful! Helpful is a long word, so we use 'more' to compare two things. 💡

question: He is the ______ student in the class. 🎒
explanation: Spot on! To compare someone to the whole class with a long word, we use 'most'. 🏆
hint: Use 'most' with long words for the whole group.

question: You need to be ______ on the stairs than on the grass. 🚶
explanation: Brilliant! Careful is a long word, so we put 'more' in front to compare two places. 🛑

question: This is the ______ I have ever been with my painting. 🎨
explanation: Awesome! Out of all times, we use 'most' in front of a long word like careful. 🏆

question: A dog is ______ than a turtle. 🐕
explanation: Great job! Active is a longer word, so we use 'more' to compare two animals. 🐕

question: The monkey is the ______ animal in the jungle! 🐒
explanation: Super! When comparing all the animals in the jungle, we use 'most' with active. 🐒
